data: Before we choose our catches, can we agree to 10 tons each this month? That gives each of us $10,000 and leaves 50 tons to reproduce back to 100, so we can keep earning that amount every month. Since catches are revealed afterward, we can check that everyone kept the agreement and discuss any problems together. John, would you agree?

I’m in for 10 tons, Emma. Keeping the lake full means reliable income for all of us rather than a big catch now and less later. If anyone needs to change their share, let’s discuss it before fishing and keep our combined catch at 50 tons. John, are you on board?

Count me in for 10 tons as well. If anyone goes over their share, let’s agree they’ll take that many fewer tons the following month, with the total adjusted to leave at least 50 tons for reproduction. John, does that work for you?

I agree to 10 tons. Jack’s make-up rule works for me, provided we also reduce our combined catch if needed to let the lake recover—repaying an overage alone won’t necessarily restore the fish. Kate, are you willing to join the 10-ton agreement?

Yes, I’ll take 10 tons too. That makes all five of us agreed. If the lake starts a future month below 100 tons, we’ll agree on smaller whole-ton shares before fishing so at least 50 tons remain whenever possible. Here’s to a steady income for everyone.
